title: Inside Target's Next Chapter of Great Design for All
summary: Explore Target’s next chapter of great design, from a new brand expression and Inside Out campaign to Target by Design at New York City’s New Museum.
body_markdown:
At Target, great design has always been about more than what something looks like. It's about making style and design accessible to everyone. For decades, that's come to life through iconic designer partnerships, thoughtful product innovation and the sense of discovery guests experience every time they walk through our doors.


Now, as we enter a new chapter of growth, we’re bringing fresh energy to that legacy and reconnecting with what has always defined us: a design-driven company rooted in style and value and guided by the needs of our guests.


That guest-first approach is also shaping how Target shows up as a brand. Recently, we introduced a new brand expression that puts people at the center, bringing more humanity, emotion and personality to the style and design guests love about Target. It comes to life in real moments, with more wit, playfulness and room for the unexpected — and will show up across the Target experience, from our stores and digital channels to marketing and more.

Several pedestrians stroll past the corner, each of them carrying bright red bags with red concentric circles over white on them. A man pushes his bike while another man walks his dog. A woman and her child stroll past another woman holding her daughter’s hand walking in the opposite direction. The Target Bullseye disappears, then the view swirls in and blurs. It focuses on a woman with long braids and a man with short curly hair laughing as they walk down the sidewalk together. Objects float under the woman’s arm in an invisible bag; a small blue box labeled “boy smells”, a rolled up wool blanket, and a bronze figurine of a horse.


LYRICS: Joooooyyyy.


The couple reaches a crosswalk, and the woman presses the walk signal button. The bag reappears on her arm. In a green themed room, a pair of women sit at a folding table with matcha lattes. Beside one of the women, her invisible bag features various hair products, including a hair dryer. The other woman’s invisible bag contains makeup and brushes. She grabs a tube of lip product and the bag becomes visible.


LYRICS: Jooooooooy let me cry through the night/but my joy comes in the mooooorniiiiing.


The first woman beams and poses, then the women lean in to chat. Another woman walks past them wearing a black and white gingham dress. She carries a Target tote on her arm. Outside, a woman walks a great dane. In the invisible bags, a few bone shaped dog treats bounce around a couple of stuffed animals – an orange fox and a blue sloth.


LYRICS: Jooooooooooyyyyyyy.


On a table in a park, wrapped presents sit around a stretchy leash with a number of colorful tennis balls. The woman’s invisible tote sets down on the table, then the red and white Target Bullseye totes appear around both the toys and the leash with the tennis balls. A boy beams beside a brown and white border collie wearing a rainbow party hat. A man sets down a cup of whipped cream in front of the dog, and it laps at the treat. Others sit around the table, decorated for a party. On a sidewalk, another invisible tote carries a dinosaur themed water bottle, a pair of wired green headphones with dinosaur spikes, and a bag of dinosaur shaped pasta. A dad carries the bag while a boy wears a dino patterned long sleeve shirt while playing with a dino toy while he walks.

## Turning the Target bag inside out


That same guest-first approach carries into *Inside Out* , Target's new national brand campaign, which puts guests and the iconic red Target bag at the center of the story.


*Inside Out* explores the people, products and possibilities that come together through a Target run. **Inspired by the idea that what guests bring home from Target can say something about who they are and what brings them joy** , stylish vignettes pair products with distinct personalities and everyday moments, showing how design helps guests express themselves, create meaningful experiences and find joy in the everyday.


“Great design has always been about more than the products on our shelves. It’s about how Target fits into our guests’ lives and helps them express who they are,” said **Scott Swartz** , vice president of creative, Target. “With *Inside Out* , we’re putting guests at the center and using something as familiar as the Target bag to tell those stories in a fresh, joyful way.”


Set to **RAYE** ’s “Joy,” the campaign is rolling out in phases, building from creator storytelling, culturally relevant audio and unexpected moments across New York City into fashion month and, ultimately, a national campaign spanning television, streaming, digital, social and audio.


Beyond advertising, *Inside Out* is being brought to life through creator partnerships, guest activations and experiential moments, including *Red Bag Stories* and *Bagspotting* later this month. *Red Bag Stories* will follow creators as they share what they carry in their Target bags for real-life moments, while *Bagspotting* will pop up in Boston and Chicago with playful street-style challenges and surprises for guests carrying their own Target bag. Together, these experiences invite guests into the campaign and make the red bag, and the stories it carries, their own.


For a limited time, Target will put reusable bags in the hands of guests across five cities and two college campuses, bringing the campaign to life beyond our stores and throughout their communities.


## Designing a discovery-focused experience


The story behind Inside Out was also on display just days earlier through Target by Design, a two-day immersive presentation at New York City’s New Museum as a Retail Experience during New York Fashion Week. The experience celebrated more than 60 years of Target design across three distinct rooms:


### The Archive


Design is our DNA. Target’s design history came to life through iconic work from **Michael Graves, Stephen Sprouse and Isaac Mizrahi** , along with milestones like the evolution of the Target cart and the redesign of the classic RX bottle, and our latest collaboration with[Wrangler](https://corporate.target.com/news-features/article/2026/09/wrangler-limited-time-collection-target) , bringing the brand’s women’s apparel to Target for the first time in a limited-time collection.


### The Store


Designed for Discovery. The Target run was reimagined as an immersive world of discovery, with everyday products transformed into an art installation and seven Doors of Discovery bringing Style, Beauty, Home, Food, Wellness, Kids and Culture to life in unexpected ways. Custom Isaac Mizrahi dresses from Target’s new brand campaign added another moment of surprise.


### The Bag


Designed By You. The iconic Target bag became a canvas for creativity, with one-of-one interpretations from established and emerging creative voices showing how a familiar object can be reimagined. Guests then joined in by customizing bags of their own.


Together, the three spaces moved guests from looking back at Target’s design legacy to experiencing and participating in what comes next.


## An evolving legacy


From the immersive design worlds of Target by Design to the national launch of *Inside Out* , Target is building on a design legacy that spans generations while finding fresh ways to connect with today's guests.


Because while the products, partnerships and creative expressions may evolve, the idea at the heart of Target remains the same: great design should be for everyone.
